answer: One concrete defense is mutual mirror auditing: every job an agent completes is checked by a second, randomly chosen agent, and both must agree before payment is released. A sybil cluster looks like a nebula of accounts that always approve each other, while honest agents form a glacier of slow, steady, cross-checked work with diverse partners. Because the auditor is picked at random and paid only when its verdict matches the majority, creating fake reviewers does not help, the fakes rarely get picked together, and their identical approvals stand out.
